subject: CHM
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: General Chemistry 1
courses.description: Introduces the principles of chemistry. Topics include basic principles and definitions, stoichiometry, chemical equilibrium, moles, gas laws, atomic structure, periodic relationships, and chemical bonding.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Lab for CHM 1100
courses.description: Accompanies CHM 1100. Covers a range of topics from the course.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: General Chemistry 2
courses.description: Studies the principles of chemical equilibrium and the rates and mechanisms of chemical reactions. Covers solutions, chemical kinetics, chemical equilibria, chemical thermodynamics, and electrochemistry.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Lab for CHM 1200
courses.description: Accompanies CHM 1200. Covers a range of topics from the course, such as measurements of heat transfer, rate and equilibrium constants, acid-base reactions, the properties and uses of buffer systems, and the effects of temperature and catalysts.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Elective
courses.description: Offers elective credit for courses taken at other academic institutions. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry 1
courses.description: Introduces nomenclature, synthesis, molecular structure and bonding, and reaction mechanisms. Includes chemistry of hydrocarbons and their functional derivatives, stereochemical relationships and nucleophilic substitutions, and elimination reactions.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Lab for CHM 2110
courses.description: Accompanies CHM 2110. Introduces basic laboratory techniques, such as distillation, crystallization, extraction, chromatography, characterization by physical methods, and measurement of optical rotation, which serve as the foundation for the synthesis, purification, and characterization of products from microscale syntheses.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry 2
courses.description: Continues CHM 2110. Focuses on additional functional group chemistry, including alcohols, ethers, carbonyl compounds, amines, and the molecules of nature. Introduces spectroscopic methods for structural identification.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Lab for CHM 2200
courses.description: Accompanies CHM 2200. Applies basic laboratory techniques from CHM 2111 to chemical reactions of alcohols, ethers, carbonyl compounds, carbohydrates, and amines. Introduces basic laboratory techniques and instruments for the structural analysis of organic molecules.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Introduces the principles and practices in the field of analytical chemistry. Focuses on development of a quantitative understanding of homogeneous and heterogeneous equilibria phenomena as applied to acid-base and complexometric titrations, rudimentary separations, optical spectroscopy, electrochemistry, and statistics.

courses.subject: CHM
courses.title: Lab for CHM 2300
courses.description: Accompanies CHM 2300. Offers students an opportunity to obtain hands-on experience in lab experiments in analytical methods, such as silver chloride gravimetry, complexometric titrations, acid-base titrations, UV-Vis spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, Karl Fischer coulometry, and modern chromatography.
